Row.Text: Washington rides between the capital and distant settlements. In each swamp, his mind sees canals. In each meadow, he sees planted fields. But the mind can only do so much; there needs to be organization to make this vision real.
Order comes from the landed and educated. Organize a House of Burgesses in the capital.
The House of Burgesses is established: a chamber where the educated landowners can gather, debate, and have their voices heard.
Have a Gold Building and at least 15 Population in {1_capital}.
Order comes from the people. Organize town meetings in each settlement.
Some meetings are held in churches, some in stone halls, and some in barns. Nonetheless, they are held.
Have 4 Towns with a non-default Focus.

Late into the night, hunched together in a candlelit room, Washington and his closest friends go over their plans. Here, in the informality of Washington’s dining table, voices are raised in debate, argument, and sometimes laughter.
Formalize a cabinet of advisors: advisors on science, diplomacy, culture, warfare.
What was an informal collection is now formal: friends have become secretaries; areas of interest have become departments.
Have a Settlement with an Altar, Barracks, Garden, Library, Market, and a Monument.
Washington needs friends, not formal advisors.

Washington’s lands are a mosaic of small settlements – each town meeting seemingly sovereign in the wilds. Between the towns, small farms and homesteads govern themselves, acknowledging Washington’s authority in name, but fiercely independent.
This lack of unity invites dissolution.
New infrastructure means greater integration. Washington’s lands will be unified.

Washington is no ruler. He cultivates. Just as his people thrive, he arranges the gardens of his homestead, and spends as much time managing its affairs as that of the state. New villas spring up, built on the model of Washington’s estate, but now land is getting scarce.
Would-be cultivators will have to find their own place to settle.
Washington can help foster new settlements. Set up a company for the organized development of the hinterlands.

The fenland extends out, its black soil too acidic and wet for crops, its mud a clutching impediment to boots, and its snakes an open menace to hunters. The only residents of Washington’s lands that seem to admire it are the biting flies, who swarm there in abundance.
The swamp could be reclaimed from the water. Begin digging a drainage ditch.
The swamp serves its own purpose.

George Washington is a strategist and planner. He thinks in lines and rules, standards and metrics. At his estate, the crops extend in long orderly rows, irrigated by well-planned canals. In his office, are lines of policy. In each, there are the echoes of natural law.
Foreign goods pile high on the docks, unsold. Merchants report visits from a group calling themselves the “Sons of Liberty,” pressuring them into boycotts. Tensions ride high.
Imports float in the harbor. Boycotts are now patriotic.
Start 5 Sanctions. -4 [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS] Happiness in all Settlements while quest is active.
Condemn the terrorists, and do not fear their retribution.

Washington does not fear war. But conflict must be a final resort. His Cabinet has sent to him a proposed diplomatic course of action to resolve conflicts with his neighbors… though his people may see it as a show of weakness.
In the House of Burgesses, Washington is called all manner of things. But he knows the future is secure - for a time.
Foreigners arrive in Washington’s city. Their customs are strange, their faith unknowable. Newcomers move in small groups down the streets, wary of the suspicious glares cast by the locals.
Washington assures them, “here, we offer no bigotry and no persecution to those who would join our union.”
Though elsewhere may be in chaos, here, in Washington’s country, there is peace for all.
Be in the top 75% of Players in [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS] Happiness per Turn for 10 turns (non-consecutive).
Encourage the strangers to adopt local ways.

The line for the moneychangers stretches through the city square, the groans of pack animals and the grumbles of merchants waiting their turn mingling into a murmur of irritation. But it is the same each morning: each city has its own paper currency, and each person doing business must pay. The commissions on exchanges are highly profitable.
There must be one {1_civilization_adj} currency, minted in the capital. Find the gold to mint it.
With a centralized currency, there is a centralized banking system. Trade flows.

Snow brings silence over the army camp, and a full contingent becomes a blur of white on white. Tents lie hidden under drifts of snow, and the march of iron-shod feet becomes a muffled crunch-crunch. The hunger is entirely silent.
The story of survival against nature’s fury serves as a lesson for commanders in the field.
Freezing soldiers learn how to survive in the cold.
Infantry Units gain immunity to Damage from Blizzards.

Caravans of refugees from neighboring wars enter Washington’s lands – first one, then another. Dust-streaked faces and wounded veterans present hands callused from holding swords and long for silence and peace.
This is an opportunity that is too good to pass by. Press them back into service.
War-weary veterans head back to the front. A new front; the same war.
Declare War on a Player in your Homelands within {1_turn_timer}.
Washington declares his lands neutral territory.

Washington envisioned a land of men of dignity, where personal grievances were set aside for the good of the nation. But he is confronted now with factions – political parties set on their own promotion.
Abolish political parties. But prepare for the ramifications.
“To be a member of the nation,” Washington proclaims, “must always exalt the just pride of patriotism more than any personal loyalty.”
Research Nationalism. -9 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold in all Settlements while quest is active.
Rail lines stretch across Washington’s land, and with each turn of the driving wheel, Washington’s citizens are pulled one more step further from the centers of power, away towards the fringes.
With threads of steel, with needles of steam, the nation is knit together.
Have a Rail Station in every Settlement.
The river crossing is treacherous in the dead of night, but Washington stands at the prow of the boat, eyes straining into the darkness. The night can hide opportunity as much as danger.
By the dawn’s early light, the Americans’ flag is no longer there. The British take the field, and a song goes up among the troops in praise of their leader, George Washington.

Washington’s mood has been dark, his speech oddly stifled. His cabinet of advisors receive sharp retorts to even the simplest questions. When, finally, one presses him as to what his concerns are, Washington mutters in a low voice, “gum splinters.”
Commission a new set of teeth made of gold.
A grill of gold, if you will have it, sirs.
Commission a new set of teeth made of tropical hardwood.
Washington’s new teeth are made of blood-red mahogany. His smile is disturbing, but he says it improves the flavor of his food.
Commission a new set made of ivory.
Washington trumpets about his new teeth and will not stop. His cabinet claims his nose has grown longer.
Commission a new set of teeth made of human teeth. Source unknown.

War is expensive. It manifests in dead and missing men, but it also brings debt, taxation, and a burden that falls especially upon those least likely to see any of its yields. An outlying settlement, fed up with spiraling costs and rising taxes, refuses to pay.
+1 War Support on all wars, but {1_reward} in Towns.

Another letter from the Marquis arrives, asking for Washington’s advice in matters of state. And another, asking for advice in matters of fashion. And another, asking Washington what caliber of musket ball is best for firing at light infantry from two hundred yards. And another…

In the town square, a British diplomat is dragged from his embassy by a raucous crowd. Amidst laughter and not a little wine, the man is dragged to the center, where hot tar is poured upon him, and a basket of chicken feathers. The British are outraged, but Washington’s people find it hilarious.
The British are finally revealed to be chickens.
{1_reward} in Cities, but -10 Relationship with Great Britain.

Washington is not a king. The Privy Councilor places a crown of laurels on his brow, but he is not a king. His sword is gold-hilted and encrusted with jewels, but he is not a king. He claims he is an ordinary citizen, just like anyone in his lands. “Yes,” says his chief courtier, “m’lord.”
Adopt the title of Emperor. That, at least, is not a king.
Reject the crown. Reject the sword. Reject the title.
{1_reward} in all Settlements, but change Government to Elective Republic.
